title: French Onion Soup
subtitle: slow-cooked onions, rich beef broth, melted gruyère
excerpt: Onions cooked low and slow until deeply golden form the base of this classic French bistro soup. A rich beef broth goes in, then the whole thing is topped with toasted bread and gruyère and finished under the grill. It takes patience, but most of the time is hands-off.
sourceNotes: A French bistro staple, served in ceramic onion soup crocks throughout France. The dish became popular in Britain and America through mid-century French cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the soup base without the bread topping. Reheat and add fresh bread and cheese before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the soup base and freeze in portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The soup base keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Top with bread and cheese just before serving.

content.text: The onions need at least 45 minutes over low heat to turn properly golden. Do not rush this step -- pale onions give a bland soup. Stir every few minutes and let the heat do the work.

items.prepNote: use 4 thick slices of baguette, toasted

content.text: Melt the butter with the oil in a large heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Stir to coat.
Cook the onions for 45 to 55 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. They should turn deep golden brown. Lower the heat if they colour too fast.
Pour in the wine and scrape up any bits from the bottom. Cook for 3 minutes until the wine mostly evaporates.
Add the stock, bay leaves, thyme, and sherry vinegar. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and thyme.
Season with salt and pepper. Ladle into ovenproof bowls set on a baking tray.
Place a slice of toasted baguette on each bowl. Top generously with grated gruyère.
Place under a hot grill for 3 to 5 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Serve immediately.

items.fix: Lower the heat and add a splash of water to deglaze the pan.

items.cause: Onions were not caramelised long enough
items.fix: Cook the soup uncovered for another 10 minutes to concentrate the flavour.

items.cause: Cheese was too cold or grill not hot enough
items.fix: Bring the cheese to room temperature and make sure the grill is fully preheated.

content.text: French onion soup has been a staple of Parisian bistros for centuries. It was long considered peasant food, built from the cheapest ingredients: onions, bread, and a little cheese. The version most people know today -- with the gratin topping -- became fashionable in the 19th century. It is now one of the most-ordered soups in France and far beyond.
